doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Dixieland versus traditional New Orleans music
summary: Why New Orleans musicians avoid 'Dixieland', the Original Dixieland Jazz Band contract, and the structural rules of traditional playing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: proved to be a long history of New Orleans musicians either over or under-valuing themselves he asked for way too much money. So the first jazz record contract went to five white guys from Kansas City called the Original Dixieland Jazz Band and that was the moniker for the music. We call it traditional New Orleans music. The thing about Dixieland — it sounds like circus music [scats]. For us there’s when to play two [scats] and that has to do with the second line in the streets, when to play two and when to play four on the bass, and the drummer would walk in four. And those sections, like in trios, when I say trios I’m talking about “Original Dixieland One-Step” [scats] you know they’re like John Philip Sousa type marches and they have different key areas but [scats] they’re very specific parts. There’s time — how many times do you repeat each section? When do you play two? When do you play four? These are all part of traditional New Orleans music that Dixieland players rarely if ever acknowledge. So that’s the basic difference.
